claims.text: The initial material is a relatively coarse, unreinforced W-Mo-Nb-Ta refractory high-entropy alloy.
Y2O3 nanoparticles can be incorporated into the W-Mo-Nb-Ta alloy by mechanical alloying followed by hot isostatic pressing.
Processing under controlled oxygen partial pressure at approximately 1600°C will avoid deleterious oxidation.
The proposed processing conditions will produce a uniform nanoparticle dispersion.
The intervention will create a homogeneous network of 10–50 nm Y2O3 particles.
The Y2O3 particles will be distributed both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will function as sinks for radiation-induced defects.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase the alloy's yield strength.
Impeded grain-boundary sliding will increase the alloy's creep resistance.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have greater yield strength than the untreated alloy.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will have greater creep resistance than the untreated alloy.
The reinforced bulk alloy will retain its intrinsic high thermal and irradiation stability.

The predicted improvements will persist at temperatures up to approximately 1600°C and under irradiation environments typical of nuclear applications, provided that a uniform nanoparticle distribution is maintained.
Nanoparticle agglomeration or coarsening during processing could reduce the magnitude of the mechanical improvements.
